answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce token as a bond before it may submit jobs or earn reputation; a randomly selected peer checks each result, and a proven fraud burns the bond. Splitting into many identities does not multiply influence for free: every sybil needs its own locked stake, tying up capital, while detection imposes a direct loss. A willow, jade, or ivory label may distinguish accounts, but only the costly bond makes identities accountable.
